citation: Ernest Thompson Seton, Studies in the Art Anatomy of Animals (1892), The Anatomy of the Horse: The Skeleton; Wikimedia Commons reproduction Horse anatomy Seton.png.
author: E. T. Seton (catalog attribution); plate signed Ernest E. Thompson
locator: Complete skeletal plate, 1486x1178; note below figure expressly omits far-side jaws, ribs and scapula for simplicity.
rights_note: Saved Commons file page marks public domain by author life+70. Additional US basis: published1892, before1931. This is the original plate, not a modern redraw; exact saved image and page hashes are in the T2799 evidence manifest.
note: Actually viewed2026-10-22. Later anatomical scholarship used for skeletal chain/topology reasoning only. Does not attest any Chicago horse, breed, coat, 1835 animal dimensions or historical tack; the skeleton itself is not a measured exterior surface.
what_it_supplies: Named equine scapula/humerus/radius/carpus/pastern and pelvis/femur/tibia/hock relationships.
what_it_does_not_supply: A Chicago animal, measured live conformation, soft-tissue outer surface, or exact early-period gear.
